bull_bear.body:
- Dividend per share held flat at Rs 3.0 for FY23, FY24, FY25 and FY26, with dividend payout ratios shown as 17%, 13%, 18% and 37% across those years.
- Networth (Rs Bn) progression shown as 13.5 (FY23), 17.9 (FY24), 25.1 (FY25), 30.7 (FY26) and 33.1 (Q1FY27).
- Return on Equity (%) shown as 20, 33, 33, 20 and 21 for FY23 to Q1FY27, with Q1FY27 annualised.
- Capital is being deployed into the Net Margin Trading Facility book, which grew to Rs 17.9 Bn in Q1FY27 (up 24% q-o-q) from 4.9, 9.2, 9.3 and 14.5 (Rs Bn) in FY23-FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Described as a 'Leading Full-Service Financial Services Platform' with Assets Under Management and Custody of INR 2,571 Bn and net worth of INR 33.1 Bn, with a 'strong capital base supporting diversified financial services businesses'.
- Research is the stated competitive core: a team of 48 research professionals covering 317+ stocks across 20+ sectors, which the deck says 'represents over 68% of India's market capitalisation'.
- Investment banking claims 'India's Top Investment Bank In FY 2026, for IPOs Across Sectors', '1 in Every 4 Mainboard IPOs in FY '26' and a '25.9% Market Share of Total No. of Mainboard IPOs'; it also states it 'Secured #1 position in the FY2026 IPO league tables'.
- Lineage from 1995 (Probity Research), internet trading in 2001, institutional equities/research in 2007, investment banking in 2008, holding-company demerger into IIFL Securities / IIFL Finance / 360 One Wealth over 2019-2022, and re-branding as IIFL Capital in 2024.
- Governance framed as a moat: board with 50% independent directors and 'clear separation of roles between Chairman and Managing Director'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Fairfax acquisition] Fairfax India Holding Corporation, through FIH Mauritius Investments Ltd. and its affiliate, has proposed to increase its shareholding in IIFL Capital to at least 51% through a preferential issue of equity shares aggregating ~Rs 2,000 crores at Rs 350 per share, an open offer, and arrangements with existing promoters, subject to customary regulatory approvals; shareholders approved the preferential issue on June 01, 2026.
- [Promoter structure] On completion Fairfax 'will join the Promoter Group alongside the existing promoters, ensuring continuity of leadership, institutional knowledge, and entrepreneurial execution', and FIH Mauritius Investment Ltd. will have a right to nominate two Directors, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.
- [Renaming] The company is 'IIFL Capital Services Limited (Formerly IIFL Securities Limited)', re-branded as IIFL Capital in 2024; every page carries a 'Strictly Private And Confidential' marking.
- [One-offs flagged] Footnotes to the results state FY26 includes a one-time statutory impact of the new labour code of Rs 71 Mn and a gain on sale of property of Rs 897 Mn.
- [Board] Chairperson and Independent Director is Ms. Rekha Warrier (over 3 decades at the Reserve Bank of India, incl. Regional Director for West Bengal & Sikkim); R Venkataraman is Managing Director and Co-Promoter of IIFL Group.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: IIFL Capital Services (formerly IIFL Securities) positions itself as a leading full-service, research-led capital markets platform spanning Affluent/HNI/UHNI broking, wealth management and distribution, investment banking and institutional equities, now being recapitalised by Fairfax India moving to at least 51% shareholding.

open.item: Hopes to see some cost-to-income benefit from H2 as exchange volumes are strong, but continued wealth investment this year will keep affecting the ratio.
Expects the second half of FY26 to be better, supported by policy stability, demand growth, lower GST rates spurring consumption and benign liquidity.
Unlikely to launch a mutual fund in at least the next 12 months based on board discussions.
Asset management AUM roughly Rs. 800-900 crores (FinTech fund, derivatives-advantage fund, repositioned equity fund) expected to easily double in the next one year.

Flagged RBI regulations effective 1st July 2026 will cause a short-term impact from increased working capital/margin requirements; marginal for the company (no prop trading), higher F&O cost for clients.
Currently ~50 wealth RMs and ~300 affluent/PCG broking RMs; focus is to increase wealth RM headcount in FY27 (no specific number given, last year was a difficult recruitment year).

Believes the ~Rs. 3,000 crore net worth (grown from ~Rs. 1,000 crore over 4 years, all from accruals) plus borrowing limits provide enough capital/headroom to grow ~20% over the next couple of years without new capital.
Hopes the wealth management business will become profitable over the next two to three years, continuing to invest and build it up meanwhile.
As of now believes it has all the elements to succeed in existing businesses (IB, institutional equities, wealth) plus in-house PMS/AIF manufacturing; no committed plans for a full-fledged AMC.
Board continuously evaluates opportunities to enhance shareholder value (potential acquisitions, new projects) and will make disclosures as and when something definitive materializes.
SEBI-driven reset of institutional equity (domestic mutual fund) yields from 1st April expected to have only marginal impact since effective yield was already close to the regulator-suggested level.

Received income tax notice for ~Rs. 56 crores combined (IIFL Management and IIFL Facilities) for the block period Apr-2018 to Feb-2025 (Rs. 27 crore ad-hoc already paid); filing appeal, holding company assessment still in progress, expects no material adverse impact.
Quite optimistic on the investment banking deal pipeline with various deals at various stages of completion, though declines an exact number.
Will focus wealth expansion on all cities where IIFL already has a broking presence (upgrading existing footprint), not only Tier II/III.
Will continue to acquire more and more of its 6,000-plus partners as a core growth strategy since branches cannot cover all of India; partners contribute ~35-40% of retail brokerage income.
As a full-service broker, needs to improve its offering in the rapidly growing algo/high-volume trader segment where it has historically underperformed due to low yield.
5paisa will continue as a separate entity with no plans to merge or take over.

Flagged that upstreaming of client funds to Clearing Corporation and potential ASBA-for-secondary-market rules could impact float income (potentially 100% if full ASBA), though no material impact at present given FDs and liquid funds.

verdicts.item: Flagged SEBI consultation paper proposing institutional brokerage cut (12 bps to 2 bps); FII brokerage not subject to cap but mutual funds are, so a reduction would impact income (quantum uncertain, not yet law).
verdicts.note: 'from 1st of April... a reset of yields that has come in because of the SEBI regulations' on institutional equity; 'the impact will be marginal because already effective yield was plus/minus the yield…

verdicts.item: With net worth ~Rs. 2,800 crores and MTF book only ~Rs. 1,500 crores, believes another ~Rs. 1,000 crores can be added to the MTF book easily (more via 50% net worth plus 50% specific borrowing).
verdicts.note: 'we are well capitalized and we have enough dry powder to grow'; net worth 'INR3,000-plus crores', but 'sequential decline in the MTF book... because of the last quarter increased market volatility' r…

verdicts.item: Targets selling about 2 lakh sq ft out of 6.2 lakh sq ft of real estate, expecting to exit Ahmedabad property in the coming quarter.
verdicts.note: 'Other income... includes a gain of almost INR90 crores on account of sale of real estate, which was held in IIFL facility'; specific 2 lakh sq ft / Ahmedabad not detailed. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Will segment customers (large base under Rs. 1 crore networth vs target segment of Rs. 5-25 crore-plus) and report the wealth business separately once it reaches critical mass.
verdicts.note: 'the HNI segment, which is the new channel which we have set up... roughly about INR12,000 crores'; separate wealth reporting emerging but full segmentation not formalized. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Flagged that anticipated mutual fund TER cuts (media talk of 25-35 bps) and inclusion of broking in TER could impact MF commissions and institutional equity business.
verdicts.note: 'reset of yields... because of the SEBI regulations' on domestic mutual fund yields; 'the impact will be marginal because already effective yield was plus/minus the yield as suggested by the regulator…

verdicts.item: Depends largely on external manufacturers for now (open-architecture model) but is building its own AIF and PMS manufacturing capability, having recruited people to scale it up.
verdicts.note: 'we have started manufacturing, in-house manufacturing, both on the PMS platform and the AIF platform, including early stage, late stage as well as a credit fund' and 'we closed our capital credit opp…

verdicts.item: Transforming the legacy retail broking business into a wealth management and financial planning practice focused on asset accumulation rather than transactional income; big mindset shift toward asset gathering to play out over the next 12 months.
verdicts.note: 'the HNI segment, which is the new channel which we have set up... roughly about INR12,000 crores'; wealth transformation ongoing but RM build slow.

verdicts.item: Focus is on the affluent segment via a Financial Planning Model, increasing cash segment and selling more financial products rather than chasing derivatives market share.
verdicts.note: 'Financial product distribution income has increased by 16%'; continued wealth/financial-planning focus but specifics not detailed.

verdicts.item: Continuing to transform legacy retail broking into a full wealth management and financial planning practice, with the people/team build-out currently underway.
verdicts.note: 'we have currently about 50 wealth RMs... Our focus is that we should increase the headcount for wealth RMs this year'; team build-out continuing but slow.

verdicts.item: Continues to try to sell real estate and will exit as and when a good deal is available; sold one Ahmedabad property last quarter.
verdicts.note: 'includes a gain of almost INR90 crores on account of sale of real estate, which was held in IIFL facility'.

verdicts.item: Distribution focus will be across all products - PMS, AIF, mutual fund, bonds, life and general insurance, wellness - expecting normalization after tax-change disruption.
verdicts.note: 'all products, AI, PMS, mutual fund and also fixed income products have seen some growth'; FPD income up 16%.

verdicts.item: Income tax authorities conducted search activity in January 2025; company cooperated fully, no subsequent communication received, and impact on financials not determinable.

wtt.tone_latest: Confident and self-funded growth narrative; gave approximate figures with caveats, owned the income-tax notices and MTF decline, and declined to comment on Fairfax stake or specific fund-use/M&A plans.
